title: NodeKit score receipt binding a score to named reference facts
description: The third layer of the reference corpus: ReferenceObservation records the facts, DesignRule states what they license, ScoreReceipt spends that licence on one real subject. Every criterion must cite at least one observationId plus specific factIds, so a score of 2 rather than 4 is answerable with 'because of this fact, on this screen' rather than with taste. humanReview lets a person disagree with a citation on the record instead of quietly rescoring: the instrument's number stays in score, the person's number goes in humanReview.revisedScore, and both survive.

ruleId.description: The DesignRule being applied. The corpus gate resolves it against the rules in the corpus; a receipt citing a rule that is not there is scoring against nothing.

derivedFrom.description: The union of every fact any criterion cites. Kept in the same shape as DesignRule.derivedFrom so the existing corpus gate resolves a receipt's citations with no special case.

scoreBasis.description: How the criterion scores compose into the single number, stated so a reader can re-derive it.

notScored.description: What this receipt did not examine. Required and non-empty, on the same principle as the gate's denominator line: a score silent about its gaps reads as total.

scoredBy.description: The instrument or agent that produced the criterion scores. Not a grade and not an approval — an identity, so the number has an author.

evidenceBasis.description: live-inspection: the scorer opened the surface. recorded-observation: the scorer worked from a dated first-party record of it, which is weaker and must say so.

ruleApplicability.description: The applicability check, written out before the score rather than assumed. A receipt that cites a rule the subject is outside is a fabricated citation with a real fact id in it.

doesNotApplyWhenChecked.description: Every doesNotApplyWhen clause of the cited rule, each answered. If any fires, the rule does not govern this subject and the receipt must not exist.

rejectedSubjects.description: Subjects considered and put down because a doesNotApplyWhen clause fired. Recorded so the next reader does not re-litigate the choice.

anchors.description: Every point on the scale described concretely, and where possible tied to an observed surface. An unanchored scale is a preference with integers on it.

citation.description: One observation, and the specific facts within it that carry this criterion's score. factIds are bare ids; the corpus gate qualifies them with observationId and resolves each one.

relation.description: How the subject stands against the cited facts.

withinRuleDerivation.description: Whether every fact in this citation appears in the cited rule's derivedFrom.factIds. False is allowed and sometimes right, but it marks a criterion reaching past the rule's own evidence — which is exactly the thing a human reviewer should be able to find and dispute. The corpus gate recomputes this flag; it is a cross-reference, not a self-assessment.

humanReview.description: A person disagreeing with the machine, on the record. decision override requires a revisedScore; affirm and abstain must not carry one.
